root_cause.note: stated by both analyses, with the same code excerpt
root_cause.value: the overflow mask in checked_shlw is 0xffffffffffffffff << 192 rather than 1 << 192, so the check does not fire and get_delta_a's numerator wraps silently inside the u256

scope_note.note: quoted from the Updates note in the fetched payload
scope_note.value: Verichains notes 'this vulnerability may affect other projects that use the same vulnerable math function'

severity.note: no severity label is published by any source we hold: the first-party page is unreadable in our payload and both analyses publish loss figures only

affected_components: Cetus CLMM clmm_math::get_delta_a (the caller both analyses identify)
finding.affected_versions: not published as a version range; Verichains decompiles the live mainnet module at 0x714a63a0dba6da4f017b42d5d0fb78867f18bcde904868e51d951a5a6f5b7f57 (module math_u256)
finding.patched_versions: integer-mate PR #7 'Fix checked_shlw' merged 2025-05-22T16:09:27Z (merge commit 06660f704c4ac1d443ab62346a46b5b60d49df33), touching aptos/sources/math_u256.move and sui/sources/math_u256.move

root_cause.note: both analyses print the same mask expression and the same intended check; we did not execute the Move code ourselves
root_cause.value: checked_shlw computes mask = 0xffffffffffffffff << 192 and tests n > mask, which is not the intended n >= 1 << 192 test, so most values greater than 2^192 pass; the subsequent << 64 then wraps silently (Move shifts do not abort), and clmm_math::get_delta_a divides the truncated numerator by p0*p1 and casts the result to u64

finding.severity_source: none of our sources publishes a severity label for this incident: the first-party report page is a JavaScript shell we could not read, and the two technical analyses publish loss figures in their titles ($260M per Verichains, $200M per Dedaub) rather than a severity
finding.summary: checked_shlw was meant to detect that a u256 overflows when shifted left by 64 bits, but tested against 0xffffffffffffffff << 192 instead of 1 << 192, so values above 2^192 passed undetected; the 320-bit product produced by get_delta_a then wrapped inside the u256 and collapsed to a tiny residue, so the token-A deposit for a liquidity add was computed as almost nothing while the LP tokens minted were not, and repeated add/remove cycles drained the pool on 2025-05-22.
finding.title: A wrong overflow mask in math_u256::checked_shlw silently truncated a 320-bit product, letting an attacker mint unbacked liquidity and drain the Cetus CLMM on 2025-05-22

finding.summary: The pattern: assigning a value to a Move reference (`*x = y`) silently converts the target's type (u8 -> u64, etc.), so a shares field written through a reference of the wrong numeric type corrupted the share total and minting became permanently impossible.
